key_insight: Flux-tunable transmon qubits can detect microscopic two-level systems with intrinsic lifetimes exceeding one second, far longer than the qubit itself.
engineering_relevance: These long-lived parasitic defects can create correlated errors, so identifying and characterizing them is important for improving superconducting-qubit stability and error-correction performance.
method: Wide-band quantum-jump correlation spectroscopy on flux-tunable transmon qubits
Pump-probe measurements at multiple qubit–TLS detunings
Estimate TLS lifetime and coupling strength from switching dynamics
evidence_signal: The abstract reports observed TLS lifetimes exceeding one second and weak qubit coupling in the kilohertz range from detuning-dependent pump-probe data.
watch_item: The microscopic origin is not uniquely identified, since the signals are consistent with standard tunneling model defects but could also reflect spin impurities or trapped quasiparticles.
paper_title: Superconducting circuits host two-level systems with lifetimes exceeding one second
